| [CASE-118](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-118.md) v5 | Two competing components with overlap ρ | From the synthesis the owner relayed on 2026-10-18, checked. The two-component Lotka–Volterra system with symmetric overlap ρ: invasion growth 1 − ρ equals λ_min(A), and κ(A) = (1 + ρ)/(1 − ρ), so overlap weakens recovery and ill-conditions the features together. Holding A fixed and setting r = (1 + δ, 1 − δ) gives the coexistence equilibrium n* = (1/(1 + ρ) ± δ/(1 − ρ)), feasible only when \|δ\| < (1 − ρ)/(1 + ρ). The same representation geometry supports coexistence under one supply and exclusion under another. | Active |

| [CASE-313](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-313.md) | Removing the core of Ito and Kaneko's network | [LEAD-065](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-065.md) asked whether [QUESTION-132](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-132.md)'s candidate case, Ito and Kaneko's network of identical logistic maps with normalized, similarity-reinforced weights ([LIT-1842](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1842.md), [NOTE-1414](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1414.md)), refills its core when core units are removed. The model was reimplemented at the paper's parameters (N = 100, a = 3.97, c = 0.12, δ = 0.1) and grown for 3 × 10⁶ steps in 12 seeds. It reproduces a core of 15.6 ± 1.2 units by the paper's snapshot criterion, and 18.2 ± 1.1 by time-averaged outgoing weight above the mean, with 1.6 ± 2.6 periphery-to-core links (paper: 2). Five arms then ran for 10⁶ steps. With the whole core deleted, former periphery units formed a new core of 17.2 ± 0.8 units. The control that deletes as many periphery units formed one of 17.0 ± 1.1. The new core had 2.9 ± 4.8 periphery-to-core links. With a random half of the core deleted, 8.8 ± 0.8 periphery units joined the 8.5 survivors. With every weight given to the core cut to 10⁻³ of its value, the core's own members made up 92% of the core 10⁶ steps later. The differentiation recovers. Which units hold the core is set by the dynamics, not fixed by who held it first. One parameter point, one system size, 12 seeds. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |

| [CASE-341](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-341.md) | Identical operators under four influence rules | [LEAD-016](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-016.md) asked for [CASE-117](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-117.md) to be run. This is a reduced version on a CPU. There are four contexts, one of them rare (p = 0.02), each a linear regression with an orthonormal target. K linear operators, identical in form and differing only by initialization, mix by context-conditioned shares. Four rules update the shares: ordinary mixture-of-experts gating (the baseline), the same gating with a load-balancing loss, the same gating with a usage bias, and a multiplicative rule driven by the collective's loss minus the operator's own. Training follows influence. Each rule was run with K = 4 (no spare operator) and K = 6 (two spare), in 6 seeds, followed by eleven test arms. Every rule differentiated, with a distinct specialist for the rare context in 6 of 6 seeds. With K = 4, participation and performance matched across three rules. A rare specialist made rare (share 10⁻³, frozen) recovered in 6 of 6 seeds under all four rules. Under the multiplicative rule its growth rate did not depend on how rare it was made. Under gradient gating it fell with the share, and from 10⁻⁵ the specialist did not recover within the window. A usage bias recovered it from any share, but also raised an incompetent copy to 0.19. With K = 6, a removed specialist was replaced by a spare in 6 of 6 seeds under every rule. A suppressed specialist then failed to return in 23 of 24 rule-seed pairs per arm, whether its training had been decoupled from its influence and whether it had kept its competence. With K = 4, nothing replaced a removed specialist. A suppressed one returned every time, even after weight decay had cost it most of its competence and with its parameters frozen. One model class, one size, six seeds. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
